slots_and_copies.name: global_header
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Always read first at boot by FUN_080323d0 via FUN_0800a4bc(0,0x18). Valid iff FUN_08032828 word-sum over 24 bytes == 0 and first 8 bytes match expected magic. If invalid, FUN_0803284c rewrites it from a ROM template and all slots are cleared.

slots_and_copies.name: slot_0
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Loaded by FUN_080327e0 slot 0: FUN_0800a4bc((0*0x14+3)*8=24,0xa0,buffer). Marked valid at SaveManager+0x28+0 by FUN_080327b4 iff FUN_08032828(buffer,0xa0) word-sum == 0. No backup copy or generation counter found; invalid slots are discarded, not recovered from a mirror.

slots_and_copies.name: slot_1
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Loaded by FUN_080327e0 slot 1: FUN_0800a4bc((1*0x14+3)*8=184,0xa0,buffer). Valid iff word-sum over 160 bytes == 0 (FUN_080327b4). No mirroring found.

slots_and_copies.name: slot_2
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Loaded by FUN_080327e0 slot 2: FUN_0800a4bc((2*0x14+3)*8=344,0xa0,buffer). Valid iff word-sum over 160 bytes == 0 (FUN_080327b4). No mirroring found.

slots_and_copies.name: tail_unused
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Never addressed by any traced read/write (24 + 3*160 = 504). Remains 0xFF in both samples.

checksums.name: header_sum16_negated
checksums.formula_detail: In .sav file domain: interpret header bytes 0x00-0x17 as 12 big-endian u16 words; valid iff sum(words) mod 65536 == 0. Stored word at 0x16 (file bytes 01 00, BE value 0x0100) equals (-sum of the other 11 BE words) mod 65536. In code, FUN_08032828 sums 12 s16 words from the RAM header image, FUN_0803284c stores -sum at RAM+0x16 (_DAT[0xb] as s16 index 11) and FUN_08032364 zeroes RAM+0x16, recomputes and stores -sum before flushing. RAM is little-endian ARM; the file-domain BE verification versus RAM-domain s16 sum implies the EEPROM serial (MSB-first) layer defines the file word byte order - see report open questions. Equivalent invariant in both samples: BE total == 0.

checksums.name: slot_sum16
checksums.formula_detail: Code-proven validation only: FUN_080327b4 computes FUN_08032828(slot_RAM_buffer, 0xa0), i.e. sum of 80 s16 words over the full 160-byte slot, and sets valid flag SaveManager+0x28+slot = (sum == 0). No slot writer or checksum setter was found in the 307 traced functions, so the stored word position is not code-proven. By analogy with the header (checksum as last word), the hypothesised stored offset is slot_base+0x9E, but this is unproven. Both samples contain only cleared/erased slots (first 8 bytes 0x00, rest 0xFF, word-sum 0xFFB4 != 0), so no valid slot sample exists to verify against.

io_driver_functions.notes: DMA3 driver (EEPROM serial transfer): saves/clears a DMA/IME control register via _DAT_08043544, programs DMA3 source=_DAT_08043554 register, dest=_DAT_08043558 register, count|0x80000000 (enable) at _DAT_0804355c (DMA3 registers at 0x040000D4 family), polls busy bit 0x8000 of DMA3 control high halfword, restores saved register. Used for both directions to/from EEPROM window 0x0D000000. Role is generic DMA, direction depends on caller argument order.

Nintendo EEPROM_V124 ReadEeprom: one 8-byte block. Args (block_addr u16, dest). Rejects addr >= *(u16*)(eeprom_config+4) (block count). Builds MSB-first address bitstream using address-bit count at config+8 (6 for 512-byte EEPROM), start bits 1,1, DMA stack->0x0D000000 (config+8 + 3 bits), then DMA 0x0D000000->stack (0x44 halfwords = 64 data bits + framing), reassembles 4x u16 from 16 captured bits each and stores them in reverse word order to dest+6..dest+0. Returns 0 on success (uRam08043580 error value otherwise).

Nintendo EEPROM_V124 WriteEeprom: one 8-byte block. Args (block_addr u16, src u16* x4, wait_flag). Expands 4x16 data bits plus address bits (config+8) MSB/LSB serial framing with start bits 1,0, DMA stack->0x0D000000 (config+8 + 0x43 bits), then polls EEPROM busy: reads 0x0D000000 bit0 and a timer register (_DAT_08043714, wrap 0xE4) with timeout accumulator 0x88; repeats per wait_flag. Returns 0 on success.
WriteEeprom wrapper thunk: returns FUN_08043628(addr, data, 1) - write with busy-wait enabled. Missed by callgraph.json (func_ alias call), mapped by textual reference in FUN_0800a524.

Nintendo EEPROM_V124 VerifyEeprom: reads block via FUN_08043564 into stack and compares 4x s16 against supplied data; returns 0 on match, 0x8000 on mismatch. Called after every write block by FUN_0800a524.

IdentifyEeprom / type select: param 4 selects the 4-Kbit (512-byte) config struct pointer, param 0x40 selects a larger config, other values select a third config and return 1; recognised types return 0. FUN_0800a59c always passes 4, matching EEPROM 4K / 512-byte media. Config struct: +4 = block count limit (u16), +8 = address bit count (u8, 6 for 64 blocks).

EEPROM session begin: saves two hardware registers (WAITCNT-family via _DAT_0800a5c8/_DAT_0800a5d0 and a config register), clears one, calls FUN_0804349c(4), returns (result == 0). Missed by callgraph.json, mapped by func_0x0800a59c textual calls in both wrappers.
EEPROM session end: restores the two registers saved by FUN_0800a59c (_DAT_0800a5f8, _DAT_0800a600).

Game EEPROM read wrapper: args (byte_offset>>3 = block, byte_length>>3 = block count, RAM dest). Begins session via FUN_0800a59c; per 8-byte block calls FUN_08043564 with up to 3 retries on non-zero return; dest advances 8, block advances 1; ends session via FUN_0800a5e4; returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.

Game EEPROM write+verify wrapper: args (byte_offset, byte_length, RAM src), both >>3 to blocks. Per block: calls FUN_08043614 (write, wait=1) then FUN_08043788 (verify read-back compare), up to 3 attempts per block; ends session; returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.

Sum16 checksum core: args (s16* data, byte_length); sums (byte_length>>1) signed 16-bit words with 16-bit truncation, returns s16. Valid data sums to 0. Used for both 24-byte header and 160-byte slots.

ValidateHeader: FUN_0800a4bc(0,0x18,SaveManager header RAM); if FUN_08032828 sum over 12 s16 != 0 returns 0 (invalid); else byte-compares first 8 RAM bytes against expected magic at iRam08032428 for 8 bytes; returns read-success flag if both pass, else 0.

CreateDefaultHeader: FUN_080289d8 memcpy 0x18 bytes from ROM template (_DAT_0803288c) into header RAM, sums 12 s16, stores -sum at header s16 index 11 (byte 0x16), writes via FUN_0800a524(0,0x18) (third argument elided by Ghidra, contextually the header RAM).

FlushHeaderIfChanged: reads EEPROM header (0,0x18) into stack, zeroes RAM header+0x16, recomputes FUN_08032828, stores -sum at +0x16, compares RAM vs EEPROM as 6x u32; if different writes RAM header via FUN_0800a524(0,0x18). Returns 1 if written, 0 otherwise.
LoadSlot(slot): FUN_0800a4bc((slot*0x14+3)*8, 0xa0, *(SaveManager+0x18)) - byte offset slot*160+24, length 160, into the shared slot RAM buffer.
ValidateSlot(slot): computes FUN_08032828(*(SaveManager+0x18), 0xa0); stores bool (sum==0) at SaveManager+0x28+slot; returns that bool.
ClearSlotBuffer: FUN_080285f0 memset(*(SaveManager+0x18), 0, 0xa0). Only used during factory-init; slot EEPROM clearing itself writes only the first 8 zero bytes per slot (see FUN_0803242c).

EXCLUDED: unsigned modulo/remainder helper (calls func_0x080438f0 on divide-by-zero). Listed in save_related_functions.c only as a seed neighbour; no EEPROM/DMA/save behaviour. Not part of the save system.

caller_chains.trigger_context: Boot / save-system init (SaveInit). Direct caller not in callgraph.json and no textual caller in decompiled.c - reached via an unrecovered indirect jumptable/state dispatch (UNRECOVERED_JUMPTABLE). Allocates the 160-byte slot buffer with FUN_08028874(0xa0) (zeroing allocator) and stores it at SaveManager+0x18, calls the FUN_0800a4b4 no-op stub, then validates the header.
caller_chains.how_mapped: Direct FUN_/func_ calls in the body of FUN_0803242c in ghidra/decompiled.c (lines 7027-7044); callgraph.json agrees for FUN_080323d0 as its callee.

caller_chains.trigger_context: Factory init branch of SaveInit, taken only when FUN_080323d0 returns 0 (bad checksum or bad magic, e.g. blank/corrupt EEPROM): create default header from ROM template, fix its checksum, write it, clear the RAM slot buffer, then for slot=0..2 write only the first 8 zero bytes at byte offsets 0x18, 0xB8, 0x158 (FUN_0800a524(iVar4,8,slot_buffer), iVar4 += 0xa0). This exactly produces the zero blocks observed at 0xB8 and 0x158 (and 0x18) in both .sav samples. Afterwards FUN_080384b0(*(u8*)(SaveManager+10)) applies header byte 10 (locale/index, hypothesis) and FUN_08032744 loads all slots.

caller_chains.trigger_context: Settings/header save event. FUN_08026658 is a state/menu handler (no traced caller; indirect dispatch) that in one branch sets a settings word to 0x14 and calls FUN_08020688. FUN_08020688 packs settings into the header RAM, brackets the flush with FUN_08036a60->FUN_080402a0 and FUN_08036a6c->FUN_08040270 (hardware register lock/unlock pair), and calls FUN_08032364 which recomputes the header checksum and writes the 24-byte header only if it differs from EEPROM.
caller_chains.how_mapped: callgraph.json lists FUN_08020688 caller as 0x08026658 and the decompiled body of FUN_08026658 contains FUN_08020688() at its settings branch; FUN_08020688 body contains direct byte stores to the header struct followed by func_0x08032364(). The settings struct base and header base absolute RAM addresses are _DAT_ pointer values not recoverable from the decompiled text.

caller_chains.trigger_context: Header unpack on load (reader side of FUN_08020688): copies header fields back into the settings struct. No textual or callgraph caller found in the 307 functions - reached indirectly. FUN_08021374 (nearby, sets settings bytes +0x10/+0x11=6, +0x12=0, +0x13=0 after FUN_0801f17c) appears to initialise defaults for the same settings struct.

fields.name: magic_ascii
fields.update_mechanism: Written once as part of the 24-byte ROM template copy in FUN_0803284c during factory init; never changed afterwards (FUN_08032364 only rewrites the whole header if other fields changed). FUN_080323d0 validates by 8-byte compare against the expected string at iRam08032428 after a successful EEPROM read.
fields.evidence: Both .sav files start 34 34 30 30 41 42 47 43 = '4400ABGC'. Code: FUN_080323d0 lines 6997-7000 byte-compare loop over 8 bytes; PACKET cold-reload probe confirms integrity failure handling.

fields.name: header_settings_group_a
fields.update_mechanism: RAM SaveManager header offsets +0x08..+0x0B. FUN_08020688 stores settings+0x10 -> +0x08, settings+0x11 -> +0x09, settings+0x13 -> +0x0A, constant 1 -> +0x0B, then FUN_08032364 flushes if changed. FUN_08021390 reverses these on load. FUN_0803242c additionally reads header+10 (decimal) as an index into FUN_080384b0 (0 selects byte 0x2C, 1 selects 0x2E - locale/language-style selector, semantics hypothesised). Individual byte semantics beyond the pack/unpack mapping are not proven; the constant 1 at RAM +0x0B is not directly observed as 01 at file offset 0x00B in either sample, so the exact RAM-to-file byte position of this subgroup remains unresolved (see report).
fields.evidence: FUN_08020688 lines 4535-4540 and FUN_08021390 lines 4586-4590 are inverse byte-store patterns on the same struct offsets; FUN_0803242c line 7043 passes *(SaveManager+10) to FUN_080384b0.

fields.name: header_counter_field_w6
fields.update_mechanism: Only observed change between the two captures at byte 0x0C (00 -> 01). No traced writer stores specifically to header+0x0C; it is covered by the header checksum (PACKET mutation probe at 0x0C confirmed integrity failure and rewrite). Semantics unknown: candidate is a counter or one byte of a packed settings word. Its +1 change is exactly compensated by the -1 change at 0x10, preserving the word-sum.
fields.evidence: Byte diff of the two real .sav files (only 2 bytes differ); PACKET probe_offset_hex 0xC with integrity_check_confirmed and reverted_to_blank_on_mutation.

fields.name: header_field_w7
fields.update_mechanism: Static in both samples; written by template copy at factory init and covered by checksum. Byte 0x0D bit7 in RAM is a packed flag (FUN_08020688 preserves low 7 bits of header+0x0D and ORs settings+0x12 << 7; FUN_08021390 reads it back as >>7), but file offset 0x0D is 0x00 in both samples so the flag is clear. Remaining bits semantics unknown.
fields.evidence: FUN_08020688 line 4537 and FUN_08021390 line 4588 operate on struct+0x0D bit7; observed bytes unchanged across captures.

fields.name: header_compensating_field_w8
fields.update_mechanism: Byte 0x10 decrements 0x10 -> 0x0F between captures, exactly cancelling the +1 at 0x0C in both LE (+1/-1) and BE (+0x100/-0x100) word sums, so the stored checksum at 0x16 does not change. Byte 0x11 (0x14 = 20) is static and in RAM is header+0x11, which FUN_08020688 writes from settings+0x60 and FUN_08021390 reads back to settings+0x60. The paired 0x0C/0x10 behaviour is consistent with two counters moving in opposite directions (e.g. used vs remaining) or a deliberately checksum-preserving pair; semantics unproven. This field is NOT the checksum: the code-proven checksum store is at 0x16.
fields.evidence: Two-sample diff; net word-sum delta 0 in both endiannesses; FUN_08020688 line 4540 / FUN_08021390 line 4590 for the +0x11 byte.

fields.name: header_erased_padding_w9_w10
fields.update_mechanism: Part of the third EEPROM block of the header (bytes 0x10-0x17 are written as one 8-byte block by the EEPROM layer). Value 0xFF is the EEPROM erased state, indicating the ROM template itself carries 0xFF here (unused/reserved) - the game writes full blocks, so RAM must contain FF FF FF FF at +0x12..+0x15. Covered by the checksum (contributes two 0xFFFF words). No writer or reader accesses these offsets individually in the traced code.
fields.evidence: Both samples; EEPROM block granularity proven by FUN_08043564/FUN_08043628 (8-byte blocks) and FUN_0800a4bc/FUN_0800a524 (>>3 block conversion).

fields.name: header_checksum
fields.update_mechanism: Stored as s16 index 11 (byte offset 0x16) of the header. FUN_0803284c: after template copy, sum 12 s16 via FUN_08032828-style loop and store -sum. FUN_08032364: zero this word, recompute sum over 24 bytes, store -sum, then flush only if the header differs from EEPROM. Validation (FUN_080323d0) requires total sum == 0. In the .sav file domain the verified form is: sum of 12 BE u16 words == 0, stored BE 0x0100 = -sum(other 11) on both samples.
fields.evidence: Python verification on both real files: BE words sum to 0x0000, computed -sum(others) = 0x0100 = stored. Code proof: FUN_08032364 lines 6946-6948, FUN_0803284c lines 7197-7202, FUN_080323d0 lines 6990-6995.

fields.name: slot_first_block_cleared
fields.update_mechanism: During factory init, FUN_0803242c writes only 8 bytes (one EEPROM block) of the zeroed slot RAM buffer at each slot base (0x18, 0xB8, 0x158). This is the empty-slot marker actually persisted; the remaining 152 bytes per slot are never written and retain erased 0xFF. Slots therefore fail FUN_080327b4 validation (word-sum 0xFFB4 != 0) and are treated as empty.
fields.evidence: Both samples show exactly 8 zero bytes at each of the three slot bases predicted by (slot*0x14+3)*8 and the 0x18+i*0xA0 loop in FUN_0803242c lines 7036-7041; all other slot bytes are 0xFF.

fields.name: slot_payload
fields.update_mechanism: Unknown. The full 160-byte slot is read into RAM and checksum-validated on boot, but no function in the 307 traced functions serializes a slot payload or sets a slot checksum (the only FUN_0800a524 slot call writes 8 bytes at init). A slot writer must exist outside the traced set or via an unrecovered indirect call. Internal field layout cannot be mapped from empty samples.
fields.evidence: Exhaustive textual search for FUN_0800a524/func_0x0800a524 and 0xa0 uses in decompiled.c; both samples contain no non-FF slot payload byte beyond the cleared first block.

fields.update_mechanism: Never addressed: geometry 24 + 3*160 = 504 leaves the final EEPROM block (64th block, offset 504) unused. No traced function reads or writes it.

Already confirmed by PACKET probe at 0xC (integrity_check_confirmed, reverted_to_blank_on_mutation, save_rewritten_after_mutation).

fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Checksum passes but the 8-byte magic compare in FUN_080323d0 fails, so header is still rejected and factory init runs. Distinguishes magic check from checksum check.

fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: FUN_08021390 copies it to settings+0x60 on load; observable as whatever that settings byte controls (unknown - watch for option/language/profile change). Then trigger a settings save (FUN_08026658 path) and confirm the value persists via FUN_08020688.

Tests the hypothesised slot checksum position at slot+0x9E and reveals slot payload parsing; if the game still treats it as empty, the slot checksum position or extra validity fields are wrong - revise hypothesis.

open_questions: Absolute RAM addresses of the SaveManager/header struct and settings struct: Ghidra _DAT_ symbols give only the ROM addresses of the pointer literals (e.g. _DAT_080323c0, _DAT_08032478), not their EWRAM/IWRAM values, so ram_addr is null throughout. Resolving requires the ROM bytes or the pointer literal contents, which are not in this workspace.

RAM-to-file word byte order: code sums s16 (little-endian ARM) from RAM, but both .sav files verify only as big-endian u16 sums in the file domain, while the magic reads as plain ASCII in file order. The EEPROM serial layer (MSB-first bitstreams in FUN_08043564/FUN_08043628) must define this mapping, but it is not fully resolved from the decompiled text. File-domain formula is verified; RAM-domain byte order is not claimed.

Exact file position of the header+0x0B constant-1 flag written by FUN_08020688: neither sample shows 01 at file offset 0x0B. Either the flag was never set before these captures, or the RAM-to-file subgroup mapping differs. Needs a capture taken after a known settings-save event.

Semantics of the paired fields at 0x0C (+1) and 0x10 (-1): they move in opposite directions preserving the checksum. No traced writer stores to either offset individually. Candidate: used/remaining counters. Needs a capture series across a known gameplay event.

Slot payload format (152 bytes per slot beyond the cleared first block) is completely unmapped: both samples are empty/erased, and no slot serializer or slot checksum setter exists in the 307 traced functions. The slot writer and the slot checksum stored position (hypothesised slot+0x9E by header analogy) require a non-empty save sample.

Direct callers of FUN_0803242c (SaveInit), FUN_08021390 (header unpack) and FUN_08026658 (settings save trigger) are not in callgraph.json and have no textual callers in decompiled.c; they are reached via unrecovered indirect jumptables. Their trigger contexts (boot state, menu state) are inferred from position and behaviour, not proven.

EEPROM config struct contents (block count at +4, address bits at +8) for the type-4 selection in FUN_0804349c are pointed to by _DAT_ literals whose values are not in this workspace. The 64-block / 6-address-bit geometry is inferred from the 512-byte media and the >>3 block addressing, not read from the struct.
Whether FUN_080384b0's header-byte-10 index (0 -> 0x2C, 1 -> 0x2E) is a language/locale selector or another table index: behaviour is code-proven, semantics are hypothesised.
